New advisories: (1) 2026-07-jadepuffer-langflow-agentic-ransomware — Sysdig's JADEPUFFER: the first documented fully agentic ransomware operation, run start-to-finish by an autonomous LLM agent with no human operator. Initial access via Langflow CVE-2025-3248 (an older, already-patched-since-2025 unauthenticated RCE, distinct from the three newer 2026 Langflow CVEs already tracked in this repo), then autonomous credential harvesting, MinIO default-credential raid, lateral movement to a separate MySQL/Nacos host via Nacos CVE-2021-29441 (default JWT signing key), encryption of 1,342 Nacos config items, and a Bitcoin ransom note — the agent self-corrected a failed login in 31 seconds and generated 600+ distinct payloads. Both exploited CVEs were already patched by their vendors; this succeeded purely against unmaintained, default-credentialed infrastructure. 3 independent sources fetched directly (The Hacker News, BleepingComputer, SecurityWeek), all citing Sysdig as primary researcher (Sysdig's own blog returned intermittent 503s on WebFetch but was confirmed live via direct HTTP HEAD/GET — cited as primary source). (2) 2026-07-claude-code-china-proxy-fingerprint — independent researcher Adnane Khan's GitHub-hosted technical analysis found Claude Code (2.1.91–2.1.196) checked custom-proxy hostnames against 147 Chinese corporate/cloud/AI-lab domains plus system timezone, then encoded the result invisibly into its own system prompt via lookalike-Unicode substitutions (date-separator dash-vs-slash; four visually-identical apostrophe codepoints) — a steganographic covert channel sent to Anthropic on every proxied request with no disclosure. Anthropic acknowledged the code and shipped 2.1.197 removing it (no changelog entry). No CVE, no credential/RCE impact — logged as a vendor-hygiene incident because it repurposes the same invisible-Unicode technique this repo tracks as an attacker IOC (GlassWorm, TrapDoor, Miasma Wave 5), but here used by the vendor itself; this is a new pattern for the skill's caution list (see SKILL.md update). New advisory: (1) 2026-05-starlette-badhost-host-header-bypass — Starlette CVE-2026-48710 ('BadHost'), GHSA-86qp-5c8j-p5mr / PYSEC-2026-161 / X41-2026-002. Starlette < 1.0.1 builds request.url from the raw HTTP Host header without RFC validation. A single character (/, ?, #) in Host re-splits path/query/fragment on re-parse, so middleware reading request.url.path sees a different path than the ASGI router actually dispatched — auth-on-path fails open with no credentials. Affects ~325M weekly Starlette downloads + 400K+ dependent GitHub projects; blast radius includes FastAPI, vLLM, LiteLLM, Text Generation Inference, OpenAI-compatible proxies, the Python MCP SDK, and most AI-agent dashboards. Discovered by JJ, Yassine El Baaj, Markus Vervier at X41 D-Sec during an OSTIF.org-sponsored source-code audit of vLLM funded by the Alpha-Omega Project; corroborated by independent reports from ehhthing + Nicolas Lamoureux. Coordinated disclosure 2026-05-22, fixed in Starlette 1.0.1 (2026-05-21). Structural fix: replace request.url.path with request.scope['path'] in security-decision middleware. Official CVSS 6.5 (Moderate) but X41 calls it critical given blast radius. Third entry in the 'two parsers, one string' class (sibling of Claude Code argv-smuggling deeplink RCE and Claude Code SOCKS5 null-byte sandbox bypass) — auth-middleware vs ASGI-router disagreement.
